history.summary: A small village shrine dedicated to Jal Devi (the water goddess) near Bavadi (spelt Bawadi in some sources). A devotional video uploaded in mid-2026 is tagged 'Maa Jal Devi Mandir Nirman, Bawadi, Todaraisingh', suggesting construction or renovation activity around that time; no published history or founding date could be found for this specific temple. FLAG: location uncertain - the CSV places it at Bavadi village in Uniara tehsil, but Bavadi does not appear in the 2011-census village list for Uniara tehsil, and the only online footprint ties the temple to Bawadi in Todaraisingh tehsil. It may be the same as 'Jal Devi (Baori Mataji)' near Baori Pond, Todaraisingh (unverified). Coordinates are a Todaraisingh-area approximation. No duplicates of other CSV rows found.

name: Jaldevi Temple, Bavadi
town_description: Bavadi (also spelt Bawadi) is a small village in Tonk district in south-eastern Rajasthan; a village of that name in Tonk district is recorded on Jat community records, though its exact tehsil is uncertain. The area around it - Todaraisingh and Uniara tehsils - is typical Shekhawati-adjacent rural Rajasthan, with agriculture, stepwells and local goddess shrines scattered among villages.

travel.airport: Jaipur International Airport, about 140 km north-east (approximate).
travel.railway: The nearest major stations are Tonk (about 35 km) and Sawai Madhopur (about 40 km), approximate.
travel.road: Reached by village roads off the Tonk-Todaraisingh-Uniara road network; a private vehicle from Tonk or Todaraisingh is the practical option.

visitor_information.opening_hours: Not published; village shrines are typically open at dawn and dusk (verify).
